body:
Overview

This page consolidates the canonical product documentation for the Unified Inference product family ("Unified Inference"): scope, PRD highlights, design decisions, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for Q4 2026. Target audience: product managers, engineering, sales, and customer success.

Product overview

Short description:
- Unified Inference is Redwood Inference's product family that provides a single API and operational surface for hosted, dedicated, and private inference. The product enables predictable latency, cost controls, and model routing for production LLM applications.

Core capabilities:
- Redwood API (text, chat, embeddings, reranking) via redwood-api service.
- Smart routing and fallbacks via routing-service (policy-based routing, region/cost/latency tiers).
- Serving runtime (gpu-runtime) with KV caching and quantization profiles.
- Redwood Optimize (optimize-service) for batching/quantization recommendations and cost simulations.
- Console (console-frontend + telemetry-backend) for observability, per-route analytics, and rollouts.

Target customers and personas:
- Platform teams: standardized inference across business units.
- Product/ML engineers: fast integration and predictable costs.
- Enterprises: Dedicated and Private deployments with SLAs and compliance.

PRD summary and high-level requirements

This section summarizes the PRD for the Unified Inference v2.3 initiative (Q4 2026). The PRD is focused on three product goals: improve tail latency predictability, reduce per-token unit cost by 15% for common workloads, and enable enterprise rollout controls for Private deployments.

Key requirements (MUST):
1) Latency SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms for 8k token sequence typical workloads on Hosted tier (region us-west-2).
2) Cost target: 15% reduction in per-token GPU cost across top 3 customer prompt flows via batching, cache improvements, and quantization recommendations.
3) Rollout controls: per-customer feature flags with canary percentages and automatic rollback for error rate > 2% in 5m window.
4) Model routing: capability to define routing policies by latency, cost, and model-compatibility fallback chain (primary -> quantized-variant -> smaller model).
5) Security/compliance: Private deployments must support KMS integration (AWS KMS & HSM) and audit logging with 365-day retention.

Nice-to-have (SHOULD):
- Autoscaling policies tuned for burst traffic with 1-minute scaling granularity.
- Auto-suggested quantization profiles per model via optimize-service.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- All new routes served by redwood-api report p95 latency below SLO in load tests for target workload distribution.
- Cost analysis dashboard shows >=15% unit cost reduction for internal benchmark prompt-sets.
- Admin console exposes per-customer rollout controls; SRE-runbook updated.

Design specs and architecture decisions

High-level architecture:
- redwood-api (stateless front-end): receives REST/SDK requests, applies auth, rate limits, and forwards to routing-service.
- routing-service: decision engine (policy store + model catalog) that selects a model variant and target serving pool based on policy.
- gpu-runtime: inference runtime deployed on GPU nodes with local KV cache and per-request routing to kernel-selection module.
- optimize-service: offline and streaming analysis that suggests batching/quantization configurations.
- telemetry-backend: collects token-level metrics, KV hit rates, and emits per-route SLO KPIs to dashboards.

Notable design decisions (ADRs):
- ADR-2026-07: KV caching semantics standardized to prefix caching with TTL=30m default and per-customer override. Rationale: reduces duplicate compute while bounding memory.
- ADR-2026-09: Default quantized model variants will be used as transparent fallbacks only when configured in a model's compatibility map. Avoid automatic silent quality regressions.

Service-level configurations (table):
- service: redwood-api | default SLO (p95): 120ms | alert threshold: p95 > 200ms for 10m | owner: eng-platform
- service: routing-service | default SLO (p95): 30ms | alert threshold: error-rate > 1% for 5m | owner: eng-platform
- service: gpu-runtime | default SLO (per-token p95): 200ms | alert threshold: p95 latency increase > 30% post-deploy | owner: eng-serving-runtime

Data contracts and APIs:
- Model catalog entry (example fields): model_id, variants[], quantization_profiles[], compatibility_map[], region_availability[].
- Routing policy DSL (example snippets):
  - match: { region: "us-west-2", priority: "latency" }
  - actions: [{ type: "route", model_id: "redwood-llama-13b-q-8", fallback: ["redwood-llama-13b-fp16"] }]

Roadmap and themes (next 6-12 months)

Themes:
- Theme A: Predictable performance (SLOs, kernel-selection improvements, p95 optimizations).
- Theme B: Unit economics (Optimize-focused recommendations, smarter batching, cache-aware pricing).
- Theme C: Enterprise readiness (Private deployment hardening, KMS/HSM, audit logs, and compliance evidence).

Quarterly milestones (high-level):
- Q3 2026: v2.2 - kernel-selection improvements, baseline quantization profiles, console rollouts UI (canary controls).
- Q4 2026: v2.3 - latency optimizations, cost-reduction features, Private deployment rollout controls, pricing update.
- Q1 2027: v2.4 - autoscaling improvements, extended model-catalog for multimodal models, expanded APAC region support.

Dependencies and risks:
- Risk: Quantization-induced quality regressions (mitigation: canary prompt-set evals + automatic rollback).
- Dependency: GPU fleet capacity for canary-wide tests (ownership: eng-sre).

Pricing & packaging notes

Objective: align pricing to unit economics improvements while preserving predictable billing for customers on Dedicated and Private contracts.

Recommended pricing changes (effective with v2.3 release):
- Hosted API (standard): token-based pricing with two bands: short-context (<=512 tokens) and long-context (>512 tokens). Suggested list prices: $0.0009 / 1k tokens (short), $0.0025 / 1k tokens (long).
- Dedicated: reserved throughput SKU with commit-based monthly billing. Example SKU: d-gpu-8k-1000 (1000 avg concurrent tokens/s) starting at $Xk/mo (finance to finalize).
- Private: base platform fee + usage. Base platform fee tiered by node count.

Cost controls and discounts:
- Suggested committed usage discounts (10-30%) for 6-12 month Dedicated contracts.
- Batching and cache discounts: customers who opt into Optimize recommendations and enable prefix-caching policy receive a 5% usage discount for the first 3 billing cycles.

Packaging guidance for sales:
- Starter (Self-serve Hosted): free credits, limited quota, standard support.
- Growth (SMB): Hosted w/ advanced analytics, monthly committed throughput option.
- Enterprise: Dedicated or Private + SLA + on-call support + compliance package.

Billing telemetry and auditability requirements:
- Per-route token breakdown surfaced in console and exported to billing pipeline daily. Owner: finance-and-legal.

Release notes - v2.3.0 (Q4 2026)

Release summary:
- Version: v2.3.0 (rolling release starting 2026-11-15)
- Headline: Predictable latency improvements, 15% unit-cost reduction on internal benchmark workloads, Private deployment rollout controls and KMS integration.

Major features and changes:
- Latency: kernel-selection tweaks and dynamic batching improvements reduced p95 by an average of 22% on target workloads (measured in internal perf-suite).
- Cost: optimize-service recommendations and KV cache TTL tuning produced a 15-18% unit-cost reduction for the benchmark prompt-sets.
- Enterprise controls: per-customer rollout flags and auto-rollback if errors > 2% for 5m. Admin UI exposed under Console > Rollouts.
- Security: AWS KMS and HSM support for Private deployments; audit logs retention configurable up to 365 days.

Bug fixes and operational changes:
- Fixed: rare KV cache eviction bug causing increased latency under high prefix overlap (ENG-1124).
- Fixed: mis-reporting of model-variant tags in model-catalog (ENG-1182).

Rollout plan and playbook (step-by-step):
1. Pre-rollout validation (owners: eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime): run perf-suite against staging with 10x production load profile. Required: perf-report passes p95 < target_margin (120ms * 0.9).
2. Canary (owners: eng-platform): deploy to 5% of traffic for 24h. Monitor: latency p95, error rate, KV hit rate, and token billing delta. Abort if error rate > 1% sustained for 10m or latency regression > 30%.
3. Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% (48h) -> 100% (72h). At each step, validate SLOs and billing telemetry.
4. Private customer enabling: opt-in via support ticket; require dry-run in customer's staging environment and confirm KMS keys and audit log pipeline.
5. Post-deploy audit (owner: product & eng-sre): 7-day report with SLOs, cost delta, and customer impact summary posted to /confluence/eng-platform/release-audits.

Command snippets (examples):
- Start canary rollout: curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts -d '{"feature":"v2.3.0","percent":5}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
- Check SLO metrics: grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/unified-inference/slo-dashboard

Monitoring & alerts (key signals):
- alert: unified-inference-p95-regression -> trigger when p95 > SLO * 1.3 for 10m. Owner: eng-sre.
- alert: unified-inference-error-rate-spike -> trigger when error rate > 1% for 5m. Owner: eng-platform.
